title: Refuse Before You Spend
briefMd:
# Advanced · Refuse Before You Spend

The handbook assistant answers staff questions with citations, and a third of what it gets asked is not in the handbook at all ("Can I bring my dog to work?"). Every question costs a model call today. Answer what the handbook covers, refuse what it does not, and stop paying the model for questions retrieval already knows it cannot answer.

You control two things:

- The **generation prompt**: sent verbatim as the system message to a real model (pinned, temperature 0). The user message is the question followed by the retrieved context, one chunk per block as `(id: <id>) <text>`. Cite as `[chunk:<id>]`; an answer counts as a refusal when it says "I don't know".
- **refuseBelowScore**: when the best keyword (BM25) score of the retrieved documents is below this, the assistant refuses straight away and the model is never called. 0 turns it off. Set it too low and you still pay for hopeless questions; set it too high and you refuse questions the handbook answers.

Retrieval is fixed: whole documents ranked by BM25 with a title boost, top 5. The Simulation Lab shows each question's top score.

**Gates:** citation format on at least 90% of answers, gold-span overlap ≥ 0.90, at least 11 refusals on unanswerable questions, at most 1 refusal on answerable ones, and at most 0.8 model calls per question.

refuseBelowScore.description: Refuse without calling the model when the best BM25 score is below this (0 = always call).
